then.text: The guides open at ten, the choir at seven, and I have the good sense to run the kettle all day between the two.
Every Tuesday somebody tries to book the stage for a tribute act. I say yes to the ones in tune.
You're the one with the key. I've been Mair, hall keeper, for forty years, and in all that time nobody's opened that door without me. I shall allow it.
Look at it. The same hall, dusted. They'd have put a rollercoaster here. A rollercoaster! Sit down, if you want. The seats are original, and have opinions.
At the far end of the hall the Rhondda and Swansea choirs file on to the stage, together.
Gwenllian, you take the altos. I'll try not to look at them.
Chin up, shoulders back. Calon Lan, from the top. 'Nid wy'n gofyn bywyd moethus': I do not ask for a life of luxury.
A hundred voices fill the hall. In the second verse a fine, deep bass comes in from the doorway: Gwilym, still in his cap lamp.
That's the Miners' Hall, then. Back where it belongs. Take these, with the valley's thanks.
Quest complete: Whose Pit Is It?

else.text: Mind the floor. Not that it needs minding, I do it myself every morning. The Hall's not open to the public yet. Are you with the Trust?

arc_hall_choir.text: Rehearsal. Do come in, but you'll be handed an alto part, and the altos are the problem. Don't tell the altos.
